prior.what_research_said:
The diagnosis under test is CONFIRMED by the prior-art record. Across 143.x/144.1/148/150.5/177, every prior phase fixed ONE path or ONE surface and enforced the fix with the two weakest layers (per-path tests + prompt/SKILL doctrine fences), never a universal render-coverage gate. The render seam was understood as agent-honored from the start, and that fact was explicitly conceded, not cured.

WHAT EACH SOURCE SAID ABOUT THE RENDER SEAM:

(1) SEED-021 (.planning/seeds/SEED-021-f7-max-keyboard-dial-atomic-render-coupling.md) is the root diagnosis. It names the exact split-render failure: 'The F.7 dial is two decoupled halves' -- the Picture (dial-presenter.cjs glyph STRING, machine-emitted) and the Live card (Larry's model tool-call, agent-honored). 'When the engine is silent, only the picture renders: triangles that LOOK interactive but accept no keys. A renderer that draws an interactive-looking control as static text, and depends on a separate model tool-call to make it real, will ALWAYS have this failure mode.' The navigator-selected cure was ATOMIC COUPLING ('No card, no picture') -- but scoped to the Phase 144 ENGINE ARM only, as an acceptance criterion on one path.

(2) 150.5-RESEARCH.md is the most precise statement of WHY it keeps regressing. Finding B 'the actual holes': hole #1 'Contract discarded: dial-presenter.cjs:261 returns contract {shape:F.1, keyboard:askuserquestion}... the ONLY production caller appends rendered.text alone... The card half is PURE PROMPT DOCTRINE (skills/larry-personality/SKILL.md). 148-VERIFICATION concedes the card is host-driven; visual confirmation only.' Hole #4 'Prose mimicry: 143.2 taught the model the full triangle text format in doctrine, so Larry can hand-paint interactive-looking triangles with no card on ANY arm... A CODE-SIDE GATE CANNOT FULLY PREVENT PROSE MIMICRY -- the plan should add a doctrine line (never draw the glyphs without firing the card) and ACCEPT RESIDUAL RISK, or scope mimicry-detection out explicitly.' This is the smoking gun: 150.5 KNEW the final step was agent-honored, knew code could only compose the gate, and consciously left enforcement to a per-path test + a SKILL doctrine fence ('no card, no picture'). The 13-gate trigger map lists gate 11 (text appended, contract DROPPED) and gate 12 (the card = model tool-call per doctrine, marked UNGATED) as 'THE DEFECT'. 150.5 fixed only the engine arm (renderEngineDecisionWithDial via appendAskUserQuestionTrailer, the SEED-020 single door) -- explicitly one path.

(3) 177-RESEARCH.md (behavioral-channel) never touched the render seam as a coverage problem at all. It worked the dial-as-investment-level / persona / calibration legs. Its render-relevant item BCH-12 was a single color-badge seam on render-v2 (signature change), confirmed 'render() has no posture arg' -- a one-surface change, not a coverage gate. The render seam regressing is simply not its subject; it is orthogonal, which is itself evidence that 177 was 'behavioral-channel only' exactly as the diagnosis states.

(4) The CIRS Part 11 PROPOSAL + REVIEW-SYNTHESIS are the explicit TEMPLATE the diagnosis points at, applied to INVOCATION not rendering. The proposal's 'Why a new Part' is almost verbatim the diagnosis: 'contextual invocation has been wired and has REGRESSED multiple times (Phases 143.x, 144.1 RETRO-07) because the governing contract lived nowhere -- only in an orphaned, WARN-only gate. A moat-level doctrine governed by a footnote is the failure mode this Part closes.' R2 (born-wired: 'a new/modified surface fails the gate CLOSED') and R9 ('Enforced, not aspirational... warn->report, then hard-FAIL') are precisely the invocation-layer cure. The synthesis ratified R2 born-wired as 'a genuine improvement over coverage-as-a-number.' CRITICALLY: nowhere in the Part 11 proposal, the three reviews, or the synthesis is there any mention of a RENDERING-layer twin of R2/R9. Part 11 governs SUPPLY (which capabilities are wired/trigger/chain); it is silent on whether a reached gate actually FIRES as an interactive card. The diagnosis's claim that 'the TWIN gate for RENDERING was never built' is correct: the proposal scoped itself to invocation and the reviews never raised rendering.

(5) The Tri-Polar render-proof was repeatedly DEFERRED, never built into a gate. CONNECTOR-CONTRACT.md and the 155-ignite work treat Desktop/Cowork as 'no AskUserQuestion card guarantee' and ship prose 'degradation scripts' verified by a grep count (>=3 occurrences of the word 'degradation'), not by a render proof. BIRTH-FLOW-BRIEF.md constraint 9: 'every gate needs a Desktop conversational degradation script (no AskUserQuestion card guarantee; render proof V8 DEFERRED).' So the cross-surface render guarantee was a known, named, deferred debt.

NET: No prior research proposed a universal or born-wired render-coverage gate. The render seam was correctly diagnosed (SEED-021, 150.5) as a machine-composes / agent-fires split, was cured ONE PATH at a time (150.5 = engine arm; SEED-021 = F.7 acceptance), enforced by per-path tests + SKILL prompt fences, and the residual agent-honored risk was explicitly accepted. Phase 178 (178-CONTEXT.md, registered the SAME day as 177 code-complete, 2026-06-24) is the FIRST artifact to name the universal chokepoint -- and its own gate_impact text states the diagnosis verbatim: 'the other ~13 gate surfaces emit on honor, so the agent can render the ASCII gate body without firing the interactive card (the Phase 140 D-03 silent-failure class)' and proposes 'one atomic gate-emitter chokepoint... CI-enforced... Bare body is a CI defect everywhere, forever.' 178 GA-5 even asks the open question the diagnosis answers: 'appendAskUserQuestionTrailer writes a marker the AGENT must honor... Can the contract be made structural rather than agent-honored? If not, the SKILL doctrine fence is the enforcement.' So as of the prior record, the render-coverage gate is PROPOSED (178) but NOT YET BUILT, and the honest residual is that the final card-fire may remain agent-honored unless 178 finds a structural seam.

patterns.name: Pact consumer-driven contracts + can-i-deploy gate
patterns.takeaway: The interface a consumer must honor is serialized to an EXPLICIT on-disk contract during the consumer's own test run, then a separate provider-verification job replays it in CI; a `can-i-deploy` step blocks promotion unless the contract is verified in the target environment. Key lesson for an agent-honored step: an honored expectation only becomes enforceable when it is (a) extracted into a machine-checkable artifact and (b) gated by a job that fails the pipeline. A marker string the other side 'should honor' is exactly the implicit-contract anti-pattern Pact exists to replace.

patterns.name: Implicit-contract test harness (Pact's own framing)
patterns.takeaway: Pact explicitly distinguishes EXPLICIT contracts (serialized, verified) from IMPLICIT contracts enforced only by a periodically-run test harness that checks the real provider behaves like its double. The implicit path is the weaker analogue of 'selector-dispatcher writes a marker the agent must read.' The cure is to make the contract explicit AND run a verification harness that exercises the real producer (here: the real render surface) on every change, not prose doctrine.

patterns.name: Exhaustiveness check via `never` / assertNever (born-wired total function)
patterns.takeaway: Adding a new union variant makes the build FAIL CLOSED at compile time unless every handler is updated, because the default branch asserts `kind satisfies never`. This is the purest 'born-wired' pattern: a new capability cannot be added without wiring its handler, enforced by the type system rather than a reviewer's memory. Directly maps to the F.7 diagnosis - the missing twin is a render-side total function where every reachable gate that lacks an actual interactive-card emission fails the build, mirroring how CIRS made invocation born-wired.

patterns.name: ESLint switch-exhaustiveness-check as error (lint gate that fails build)
patterns.takeaway: An exhaustiveness ESLint rule by itself only warns and does NOT block the build; the author's fix is to add a `never`-typed default that turns it into a hard COMPILER error. The lesson is precisely the 'orphaned-WARN-only-gate' failure mode in the diagnosis: a lint/warn layer is the weakest enforcement tier; to be load-bearing it must be promoted to an error that returns a nonzero exit code in CI.

patterns.name: jsx-a11y + a11y-enforce: lint the COMPOSITION, not just the element
patterns.takeaway: Element-level lint (does a button exist) is insufficient; relationship/composition lint checks that an emitted control is actually wired to its target (e.g. `aria-haspopup=menu` must connect to a `role=menu` panel). A render-coverage gate needs the same two tiers: 'a card was emitted' AND 'the reached gate is wired to emit an interactive card on this surface.' Catches the per-surface slip (177 fixed only the behavioral channel) that an element-only check misses.

patterns.name: Snapshot / role-based render assertions that a control was emitted
patterns.takeaway: `getByRole('button', {name: ...})` throws (fails the test) when the interactive control is absent, and snapshot tests fail when the rendered DOM/serialized output diverges from a committed reference. This is the unit-level analogue of a render-coverage assertion: render the surface in the gate-reached state and assert the AskUserQuestion card is present. But note the caveat below - per-test assertions only cover the paths someone remembered to write, which is the documented failure mode across 150.5/177.

patterns.name: OPA / policy-as-code: enforcement OUTSIDE the model, deterministic, fail-closed
patterns.takeaway: Explicitly frames prompt-embedded rules as 'too fragile to rely on' because they depend on the LLM interpreting instructions correctly every time; the cure is a deterministic policy evaluated outside the agent where 'the LLM has no say in the policy decision.' This is the exact agent-honored vs machine-enforced gap. The render step today is prompt-doctrine ('no card, no picture' fences) - the fragile tier; a deterministic gate that intercepts the agent's output and rejects a turn that reached the gate without emitting a card is the machine-enforced tier.

patterns.name: ArbiterOS governance kernel: non-bypassable Arbiter Loop intercepts every transition
patterns.takeaway: A deterministic Symbolic Governor executes the agent's workflow and a 'non-bypassable kernel function intercepts and validates every state transition before executing the next instruction'; it can mandate that a probabilistic GENERATE must be followed by a deterministic VERIFY before a high-stakes action is permitted. This is the architectural ideal for the render step: the render (interactive card) becomes a kernel-enforced post-condition of reaching a gate, validated by code that owns the transition - not an action the LLM may or may not take.

patterns.name: Runtime governance 'Policies on Paths' - deterministic, prospective enforcement
patterns.takeaway: Argues the policy function MUST be deterministic (identical inputs -> identical decisions) and should evaluate the next state BEFORE it executes, making violations preventable rather than merely recorded. A WARN-only render gate is retrospective (records the miss after the fact); a born-wired render gate is prospective (the turn cannot complete as a non-card when a gate was reached). Determinism is also what makes the gate auditable and CI-reproducible.

patterns.name: Five-rung enforcement ladder / second independent observation plane
patterns.takeaway: Distinguishes documentary/attested claims from real enforcement, and adds a Rung-5 'second plane' that independently observes actual behavior at a layer the agent cannot influence, flagging the gap when the application plane SAYS it enforced but the independent plane disagrees. Maps directly to the diagnosis: code 'composes the gate' (the application-plane claim) but only the agent fires the card (the actual behavior); the render-coverage gate is the missing second plane that confirms the card actually rendered on the surface, per path, and fails when claim and reality diverge.

enforcement_techniques: Serialize the honored expectation into an on-disk artifact, then add a separate CI job that fails the pipeline if the artifact is unverified (Pact contract + provider verification + can-i-deploy). Prose/marker strings are not enforceable; extracted artifacts gated by a failing job are.

Promote WARN to ERROR with a nonzero exit code. A lint/coverage signal that only warns is the documented weakest tier; the same rule wired as a hard error (or a `never`-typed default) is what actually blocks merge.

Born-wired via total functions / exhaustiveness: make the type system or registry refuse to compile when a new reachable state (surface/path) lacks its render handler - the rendering analogue of CIRS making invocation fail-closed. Adding a surface forces wiring its card emission or the build breaks.

Fail-closed default: if the render gate cannot confirm an interactive card was emitted on a reached-gate turn, treat it as a failure (deny/break), not a pass. Matches OPA's 'fail closed by default' and the kernel's deny-on-unverified posture.

Move enforcement out of the prompt and below the agent: a deterministic interceptor evaluates the agent's output/transition where 'the LLM has no say,' converting 'agent should honor the marker' into 'code rejects any gate-reached turn lacking a card.'

Non-bypassable post-condition / 'think-then-verify' kernel: make the interactive render a mandatory, kernel-validated post-condition of reaching a gate (GENERATE must be followed by VERIFY before the turn is allowed to complete), so the card cannot be skipped.

Independent second observation plane: assert the card actually rendered on each surface (the real DOM/output), separate from the code that claims it composed the gate; when the 'composed' claim and the 'rendered' observation disagree, that gap is the test failure.

Render-coverage assertion per surface AND per path, generated from a registry rather than hand-written: render each surface in the gate-reached state and assert the AskUserQuestion control is present, with the test matrix derived from the same registry that defines surfaces/paths so a new one cannot silently escape coverage.

Deterministic + reproducible evaluation: the gate decision must be identical run-to-run so it is CI-stable and auditable; avoid an LLM-judge in the enforcement path for the binary 'was a card emitted' check (reserve LLM-judge for soft quality, not the hard gate).
tavily.synthesis:
A born-wired render-coverage gate is the structurally correct cure, and the external patterns converge hard on why. The F.7 slip is a textbook instance of the agent-honored vs machine-enforced gap that policy-as-code (OPA) and governance kernels (ArbiterOS, 'Policies on Paths') were built to close: a marker string the agent 'must read and honor' is the fragile-prompt tier those systems explicitly reject as unenforceable, and per-path tests + SKILL fences are exactly the WARN-only/documentary tier that ESLint-exhaustiveness and the ARMO five-rung ladder identify as the weakest enforcement. Every prior phase (150.5 engine-arm, 177 behavioral-channel) fixed one PATH or one SURFACE because per-path tests only cover the paths someone remembered to write - the same coverage hole getByRole/snapshot assertions have when authored by hand.

The decisive analogy is the TypeScript `never`/assertNever total function: it is precisely 'born-wired,' because adding a new variant FAILS THE BUILD CLOSED unless its handler is wired - which is how CIRS already cured the INVOCATION slip. The twin gate for RENDERING is the same mechanism applied one layer up: the render (an interactive AskUserQuestion card actually emitted on the surface) must be a kernel-enforced, fail-closed post-condition of reaching a gate, with the test/coverage matrix GENERATED from the surface/path registry rather than hand-enumerated, so a new surface or path cannot escape coverage. ArbiterOS supplies the architectural shape (a non-bypassable interceptor that validates the GENERATE->VERIFY->render transition before the turn completes), OPA supplies the determinism-and-fail-closed discipline, ARMO supplies the 'second independent plane' insight (code claims it composed the gate; an independent observation must confirm the card actually rendered, and the disagreement IS the failure), and Pact supplies the operational pattern (extract the honored expectation into an explicit artifact, verify it in a job that blocks promotion).

Two caveats keep it honest. First, born-wired only holds if it is wired at the registry/type level, not as another hand-written test - otherwise it inherits the same per-path coverage gap it is meant to kill; the gate must make 'add a surface/path' mechanically force 'declare its render coverage or break the build.' Second, the binary check ('was an interactive card emitted on a reached-gate turn?') must be deterministic and code-evaluated - an LLM-judge belongs to soft quality, never to the hard render gate, or you reintroduce the non-determinism you are trying to remove. With those constraints, a born-wired render-coverage gate is not merely a fix for one more path; it is the missing structural peer to Canon Part 11 / CIRS R2-R9, promoting rendering out of the orphaned-WARN-only state into machine-enforced, fail-closed, per-surface coverage."

refutation_attempts: (a) Is there ALREADY a born-wired RENDER gate I missed? REFUTED the existence claim, confirming the diagnosis. Inventoried scripts/: the only born-wired gates are the CIRS pair (build-connector-registry.cjs, build-orchestration-projection.cjs, check-cirs-declaration.cjs). build-orchestration-projection.cjs:113-138 EXPLICITLY classifies /mos:dashboard and /mos:splash as 'render-only ... presentation utility, not a reach-dispatched thinking surface' and EXCLUDES them - proving the CIRS gate governs INVOCATION/trigger-wire and treats render as out-of-scope, exactly as the diagnosis states. grep for any gate checking 'card emit / interactive card / fires card / render coverage' returned NOTHING in scripts/*.cjs. No born-wired render gate exists.

(b) Is the seam actually machine-enforced somewhere, not agent-honored? REFUTED. grep for 'AskUserQuestion' across all of lib/ and scripts/ (90 hits) shows it appears ONLY in comments, marker/contract/trailer STRINGS, and selector-construction helpers (appendAskUserQuestionTrailer, the F.1 host, mode hints). It is NEVER invoked as a tool call. The sole runtime consumer of askuserquestion_marker is intent-classifier.cjs:934, which re-emits it as TEXT in the turn block (return base + rendered.text + marker). The ONLY stated enforcement of 'a gate fires its card' is skills/larry-personality/SKILL.md:129 prose: 'Larry MUST fire the AskUserQuestion card ... no card, no picture' - a natural-language instruction the LLM must honor. grep for any PostToolUse/output-interceptor that validates a card was fired on a gate turn returned nothing (the one classifier.cjs:51 hit maps the AskUserQuestion event AFTER the agent already fired it - a downstream classifier, not an enforcing interceptor). Card-firing is agent-honored, not machine-enforced.

(c) Is 'born-wired render gate' the wrong cure - would it not stop the slip? Attempted to refute via the prose-mimicry caveat (150.5 hole #4: a code-side gate cannot fully prevent the model hand-painting interactive-looking triangles). This SHARPENS but does not refute: prose-mimicry is the agent DRAWING glyphs without firing a card on a turn the code never reached a gate; the diagnosis targets the REACHED-gate case (code composed the gate, agent must fire). A render-coverage gate that asserts 'every surface that reaches a gate routes through atomic card emission, born-wired at the registry/type level' is the correct structural peer to CIRS R2/R9 - confirmed by the external convergence (TypeScript never/assertNever total function, OPA policy-as-code, ArbiterOS non-bypassable kernel post-condition). The honest residual (final card-fire on a real LLM surface may stay partly agent-honored unless 178 finds a structural seam) is named by the diagnosis itself and by 178 GA-5, so it does not refute the missing-system-part claim.

(d) Is the real root cause the Phase 177 'two-front-doors ownership bug' or a deeper architecture issue? REFUTED as a substitute root cause. Read 177-CONTEXT.md:24,37: the two-front-doors bug is 'two routers over the same vocabulary (the 6 reaches, 3 postures, investment/dial axis), only one wired' - it is an INVOCATION/ROUTING ownership problem (which router decides the fired reach), explicitly 'Born-wired modifier per CIRS Part 11.' It lives on the trigger/decide side, NOT the render side. It is orthogonal to whether a reached gate fires an interactive card. So 177 is correctly characterized by the diagnosis as 'behavioral-channel only,' and its ownership bug is a different seam, not the F.7 render root cause.

Verified the F.7-dial new-gate-surface claim (177 minted a surface with no render coverage). dial-selector.cjs:216-228 renderDialShape returns { shape:'F.7-dial', hud, zones } with NO askuserquestion_marker (the docstring at :210 explicitly notes it lacks one). The F.7-dial branch (selector-dispatcher.cjs:755) is reached by NO production caller - grep outside tests shows only the dispatcher branch + the F_SUBSHAPES array. A new gate surface was minted with zero born-wired check that it routes through interactive-card emission. Confirms the diagnosis's '177 did not generalize render coverage.'

Verified Phase 178 is PROPOSED, not BUILT. .planning/phases/178-universal-gate-chokepoint/ contains ONLY 178-CONTEXT.md (no PLAN/code). grep for any atomic gate-emitter chokepoint (lib/hmi/*gate*, *chokepoint*, gate-emitter) returned nothing built. So the render-coverage gate the diagnosis names as the missing system part is genuinely absent as of the current tree - the diagnosis describes a real, currently-unbuilt hole, not one already cured.
verdict.strongest_counterevidence: The strongest counterevidence is the 150.5 prose-mimicry concession (hole #4): 150.5-RESEARCH explicitly states 'a code-side gate cannot fully prevent prose mimicry' and recommends accepting residual risk. This could be read to mean the diagnosis's proposed cure (a born-wired render gate) cannot actually close the slip, undermining the 'missing system part' framing - if the final card-fire is irreducibly agent-honored, then no gate makes it machine-enforced. However, this does NOT refute the diagnosis: it refines its scope. Prose-mimicry is the unreached-gate hand-painting case; the diagnosed slip is the REACHED-gate split-render case (code composes, agent must fire). A born-wired render-coverage gate that fails CI closed when a reachable gate surface lacks atomic interactive-card routing addresses the reached-gate case structurally, exactly as CIRS R2/R9 addressed invocation. The irreducible LLM-tool-call residual is named honestly by both the diagnosis and Phase 178 GA-5 as the open question, not hidden. The counterevidence narrows the cure's claim from 'eliminates all agent-honored render risk' to 'promotes reached-gate rendering from orphaned-WARN-only to machine-enforced fail-closed coverage' - which is precisely what the diagnosis asserts.
verdict.correction: No correction to the core diagnosis - it holds as stated. One precision refinement for the record (does not change the verdict): the cure must be wired at the registry/type level (a render-side total function / exhaustiveness check generated from the surface-path registry), NOT as another hand-written per-surface test, or it inherits the same per-path coverage gap (150.5 engine-arm, 177 behavioral-channel) it exists to kill; and the binary 'was an interactive card emitted on a reached-gate turn' check must be deterministic and code-evaluated (no LLM-judge in the hard gate). The diagnosis's own framing already implies this by analogy to CIRS R2/R9 born-wired-at-merge, but making the registry-level (not test-level) wiring explicit is the load-bearing implementation constraint that keeps the cure from degenerating into the same slip. Additionally, the diagnosis should note the irreducible residual it already half-concedes: the terminal LLM tool-call itself may remain agent-honored on real surfaces; the gate makes the REACHED-gate composition-to-emission path machine-enforced and fail-closed, which is the correct and achievable structural peer to Part 11, with the final tool-call honesty deferred as a named debt (Phase 178 GA-5).

synth.verdict: CONFIRMED. The diagnosis holds, verified against the live tree, not just the dossier. The system part you keep missing is real, currently absent, and structurally named for the first time only in Phase 178 (which is registered but unbuilt). What you have watched slip across 143.x / 144.1 / 148 / 150.5 / 177 is not five separate bugs. It is one architectural gap appearing in five places: rendering has no born-wired coverage gate, so every fix has been a per-path patch enforced by the two weakest tiers (a per-path test plus a SKILL prose fence), and a new gate surface can always be minted that escapes them. The code GUARANTEES the marker STRING is composed (selector-dispatcher.cjs:537, unconditional on every Shape F.* return). The code NEVER fires the card. The terminal load-bearing step -- Larry actually emitting the AskUserQuestion card -- lives only in the LLM reading a string. Confirmed by grep: AskUserQuestion is invoked as a tool call NOWHERE in lib/ or scripts/; it exists only as comments, marker/trailer strings, and a downstream classifier (lib/conversation/classifier.cjs:51,142) that reacts AFTER the agent already fired. This is the agent-honored-vs-machine-enforced gap, and it is exactly the class CIRS Part 11 closed for INVOCATION and left wide open for RENDER.
synth.the_missing_system_part: The rendering-layer twin of CIRS Part 11 R2/R9: a BORN-WIRED, FAIL-CLOSED render-coverage gate. CIRS made INVOCATION born-wired -- a new or modified surface fails the gate CLOSED (R2) unless it declares its trigger wiring, and R9 flipped that from WARN to hard-FAIL. There is no twin Part for RENDER. Proof it was deliberately scoped out: build-orchestration-projection.cjs:113-138 EXPLICITLY classifies /mos:dashboard and /mos:splash as "render-only ... not a reach-dispatched thinking surface" and EXCLUDES them -- the CIRS gate governs the trigger-wire (does a surface get REACHED) and treats render (does a reached gate FIRE its interactive card) as out of scope. The missing part is the machine-enforced post-condition: "any surface that can reach a Decision Gate must route through atomic interactive-card emission, declared at the registry/type level, with the build failing closed when a reachable gate surface lacks that routing." Concretely, three properties the current tree lacks: (1) the marker must be extracted into a verifiable artifact and gated by a job that fails the pipeline, not re-emitted as text the agent must honor; (2) the coverage matrix must be GENERATED from the surface/path registry, not hand-written per path, so a new surface (like F.7-dial) cannot silently escape -- this is the load-bearing constraint, because a hand-written test inherits the exact per-path coverage hole it exists to kill; (3) the binary check "was an interactive card emitted on a reached-gate turn" must be deterministic and code-evaluated, never an LLM-judge. The pattern is the TypeScript never/assertNever total function applied one layer up: adding a render surface must FAIL THE BUILD unless its card-emission handler is wired -- the same mechanism CIRS already used for invocation.
synth.prior_research_crossref: The on-disk record CORROBORATES the diagnosis and adds two complications that sharpen rather than weaken it. Corroboration: SEED-021 is the root diagnosis and names the exact failure mode -- "a renderer that draws an interactive-looking control as static text, and depends on a separate model tool-call to make it real, will ALWAYS have this failure mode" -- but its cure ("no card, no picture") was scoped to the Phase 144 engine arm ONLY, an acceptance criterion on one path. 150.5-RESEARCH is the smoking gun: Finding B hole #1 concedes "the card half is PURE PROMPT DOCTRINE," and 148-VERIFICATION already conceded "the card is host-driven; visual confirmation only." 150.5 KNEW the final step was agent-honored, knew code could only compose the gate, and consciously shipped a per-path test plus a SKILL fence anyway. Its own 13-gate map marks gate 12 (the card = model tool-call) as UNGATED/DEFECT. The CIRS Part 11 proposal states the diagnosis almost verbatim for invocation: it regressed across 143.x/144.1 "because the governing contract lived nowhere -- only in an orphaned, WARN-only gate," and NOWHERE in the proposal, the three reviews, or the synthesis does anyone raise a rendering-layer twin. Phase 178-CONTEXT (registered 2026-06-24, same day 177 went code-complete) is the FIRST artifact to name the universal chokepoint, and its GA-5 asks the open question this verdict answers: "Can the contract be made structural rather than agent-honored?" Two complications: (a) 150.5 hole #4 explicitly DEFERRED prose-mimicry as "code-side gate cannot fully prevent" and accepted residual risk -- but that is the UNREACHED-gate hand-painting case, distinct from the REACHED-gate split this gate cures; (b) the Tri-Polar render proof "V8" was a known, named, DEFERRED debt (BIRTH-FLOW-BRIEF.md constraint 9: Desktop/Cowork ship grep-verified prose degradation scripts, "no AskUserQuestion card guarantee"), so the cross-surface card-fire was never gated even where everyone knew it was missing.
synth.external_validation: External patterns converge hard on the born-wired render gate as the structurally correct cure and on why every prior per-path fix was doomed to slip. The decisive analogy is the TypeScript never/assertNever total function (dev.to exhaustiveness checking): adding a new union variant FAILS THE BUILD CLOSED unless every handler is wired -- the purest born-wired pattern, and precisely how CIRS made invocation fail-closed. ESLint switch-exhaustiveness (timdeschryver) supplies the negative proof: the rule by itself only WARNS and does not block the build; you must promote it to a never-typed default to get a hard error -- which is the exact "orphaned-WARN-only-gate" failure mode the CIRS proposal cited and the render seam still lives in (per-path tests + SKILL fences = the WARN tier). OPA policy-as-code frames prompt-embedded rules as "too fragile to rely on" and prescribes a deterministic policy "where the LLM has no say" -- the render step today IS the fragile tier ("no card, no picture" prose). ArbiterOS supplies the architectural shape: a non-bypassable kernel that intercepts every state transition and mandates GENERATE be followed by VERIFY before a high-stakes action -- i.e., the card becomes a kernel-enforced post-condition of reaching a gate. ARMO's five-rung ladder supplies the second-plane insight that maps the diagnosis one-to-one: code "composes the gate" (the application-plane claim) but only the agent fires the card (actual behavior); the render gate is the missing independent observation plane, and the disagreement between claim and reality IS the test failure. Pact supplies the operational pattern: serialize the honored expectation into an explicit on-disk artifact, verify it in a separate job, and block promotion with can-i-deploy -- a marker string the other side "should honor" is the textbook implicit-contract anti-pattern Pact exists to replace. jsx-a11y composition lint adds the one nuance: check not just "a card was emitted" but "the reached gate is wired to emit a card on THIS surface" -- the two-tier check that catches the per-surface slip (177 fixed only the behavioral channel) an element-only check misses.
synth.recommended_fix: Build the born-wired render gate, NOT another contract test -- the contract test is precisely the trap that produced the five-phase slip. Scope it as the rendering-layer peer to CIRS Part 11 R2/R9, with three non-negotiable implementation constraints: (1) REGISTRY-DRIVEN, NOT HAND-WRITTEN. Derive a surface/path registry of every render surface that can reach a Decision Gate (the F.* shapes plus any new F.7-dial-class HUD). Each entry must DECLARE either "routes through atomic interactive-card emission" or "render-only, excluded" (the same two-state ledger CIRS already uses for invocation). A build script (mirroring build-orchestration-projection.cjs) walks the registry and FAILS CLOSED (nonzero exit, hard-FAIL not WARN) if any reachable gate surface lacks the routing declaration. Adding a surface without declaring its card emission must break the build -- the never/assertNever total-function property. This is load-bearing: if you instead add one more per-surface test, you inherit the identical coverage hole (150.5 engine-arm, 177 behavioral-channel) the gate exists to kill, because a test only covers the path someone remembered to write. (2) DETERMINISTIC, CODE-EVALUATED BINARY. The check "did a reached-gate render route through the single card-emission door" must be a pure code predicate over the registry and the dispatcher wiring -- no LLM-judge in the hard gate (reserve LLM-judge for soft quality only), so it is CI-stable and reproducible. (3) FAIL-CLOSED DEFAULT. If the gate cannot CONFIRM card-emission routing on a reachable gate surface, it denies, not passes. Promote the SEED-020 single construction door (selector-dispatcher.cjs:537) from "mints a marker" to "the registry-verified chokepoint," and make Phase 178's proposed atomic gate-emitter the thing this gate verifies exists for every reachable surface. The one-time contract test (test-150-5, ACPT-06) stays as a unit-level smoke check but is explicitly NOT the gate -- the gate is the registry-level total function.
residual_risks: IRREDUCIBLE AGENT-HONORED RESIDUAL (named, not hidden): the gate makes the REACHED-gate composition-to-emission PATH machine-enforced and fail-closed, but the terminal LLM tool-call on a real surface may remain agent-honored unless Phase 178 finds a structural seam. The gate proves 'every reachable gate surface is WIRED to emit a card'; it cannot by itself prove 'the model on this turn actually called the tool.' This is exactly 178 GA-5's open question and 150.5 hole #1's concession. Honest framing: the cure promotes rendering out of orphaned-WARN-only into machine-enforced fail-closed COVERAGE -- it does not eliminate all agent-honored render risk.

PROSE-MIMICRY (out of scope, must be explicitly excluded): 150.5 hole #4 -- the model can hand-paint interactive-looking triangles on a turn where the code NEVER reached a gate. A code-side gate cannot prevent this because there is no marker to verify. Do not let the gate's scope quietly expand to claim it covers mimicry; scope it to the reached-gate case and keep the SKILL doctrine line ('never draw the glyphs without firing the card') as the named, accepted residual for the unreached case.

REGISTRY-COMPLETENESS IS THE NEW SINGLE POINT OF FAILURE: born-wired only holds if EVERY render surface is actually in the registry. If a future surface is built without registering at all (bypassing the registry entirely, the way F.7-dial was minted in 177 with no marker), the gate cannot fail on what it cannot see. The registry walk must be driven by an exhaustive enumeration of render entry points (grep/AST over the dispatcher branches), not a hand-maintained list, or the gap reopens one layer up.

CROSS-SURFACE (Tri-Polar) CARD GUARANTEE STILL DEFERRED: Desktop/Cowork have 'no AskUserQuestion card guarantee' and ship grep-verified prose degradation scripts (BIRTH-FLOW-BRIEF.md constraint 9, render-proof V8 deferred). The gate as scoped governs the CLI card path; the Desktop/Cowork degradation path needs its own render proof or the gate's coverage claim is CLI-only. Name this explicitly so it is not mistaken for closed.

ENFORCEMENT-TIER REGRESSION RISK: if the gate ships as WARN (the orphaned-WARN-only pattern that caused the original 143.x/144.1 regressions and that R9 had to flip to hard-FAIL), it will silently rot exactly as before. The gate MUST land as hard-FAIL with a nonzero CI exit from day one; a WARN-only render gate is functionally the SKILL fence with extra steps.
